mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the prior month relative to the previous month indicates monetary easing, which reduces discount rates applied to equity cash flows and increases valuation multiples, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical FEDFUNDS decline and SPX 20d return correlation
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1% over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.2 percentage points with the rate above 4.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: doc:Unemployment Rate and Equity Market Volatility
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE > 4.0% and monthly change > 0.2pp.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.5% YoY) and low unemployment (UNRATE < 3.5%) signals an overheating economy that triggers aggressive Federal Reserve rate hikes, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60d returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 3.5% and UNRATE < 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, a housing starts level (HOUST) below 1500 thousand units signals weakening consumer demand and potential economic slowdown, reducing corporate earnings growth and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where HOUST < 1500 during late-cycle expansions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) over the prior month indicates weakening manufacturing output, reducing corporate profit margins and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Industrial Production and Equity Market Correlation
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO declines by at least 0.5% over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 3.5% signals persistent inflation that triggers aggressive monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 3.5% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: In strong labor markets, a combination of payroll growth exceeding 0.5% month-over-month (PAYEMS) and housing starts below 1550 thousand units (HOUST) signals consumer spending shifts toward non-housing sectors that support corporate earnings growth, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Consumer Spending Patterns and Equity Returns
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where PAYEMS change > 0.5% and HOUST < 1550.

mechanism_narrative: In early-cycle expansions, GDP growth (GDPC1) exceeding 2.0% annualized indicates robust economic momentum that supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: doc:GDP Growth and Equity Market Performance
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where GDPC1 growth > 2.0% annualized during early-cycle expansions.
